oneOf.description: O_DIRECT, flushes honoured. Best default for most guests.
Ignores flushes: fast, loses data on host crash.

CloudInit.description:
What the seed configures. Either fill in the fields, or give complete
`user_data` (which then replaces the generated `#cloud-config`).

hostname.description: Guest host name; defaults to the VM name.

password.description:
Login password as a crypt(3) hash (`$6$…`). A plain password sent
to the API is hashed before the spec is stored.

user.description: Account to create; `None` configures the image's default user.

user_data.description: Raw user-data (`#cloud-config…` or a `#!` script), used verbatim.

model.description: CPU model; `None` uses the machine default.

DeviceSpec.description: A device added from the palette.

bus.description:
Bus to attach to (a QEMU bus id, e.g. `qui-usb.0`); `None` lets QEMU
pick the machine's default bus for the device.

props.description:
Properties the user set, typed as QEMU expects them (bool, number or
string). Unset properties keep QEMU's defaults.

oneOf.description: IDE / AHCI (q35 has AHCI built in).

slot.description:
Index used in this disk's QEMU ids (`qui-disk<N>`, `qui-dev<N>`).
Absent: the disk's position in `disks`. Hotplug pins it so a disk
keeps its ids when others are added or removed while the VM runs
(and across restarts). Must be unique within a spec.

spice.description:
Also serve SPICE on loopback for a native client (remote-viewer):
USB redirection and smoother video than VNC (M5-05).

vdagent.description: qemu-vdagent: clipboard + absolute pointer (needs guest agent).

vnc.description: Serve the console over VNC (proxied; never exposed directly).

oneOf.description: Whatever the machine boots by default (SeaBIOS on x86, built-in elsewhere).

Firmware from a descriptor, e.g. UEFI. The daemon keeps the per-VM
NVRAM copy (as qcow2, so internal snapshots work).

agent.description: Add a guest-agent channel (needs `qemu-guest-agent` in the guest).

cloud_init.description: Generate a cloud-init NoCloud seed and attach it as a CD-ROM.

name.description: File name inside the pool. No path separators.

usb_tablet.description: USB tablet for absolute pointing without guest agent.

oneOf.description:
User-mode NAT (slirp). Every attached VM gets its own private NAT
with this addressing; guests on it cannot see each other.

subnet.description: IPv4 subnet in CIDR form; `None` uses QEMU's 10.0.2.0/24.

oneOf.description:
NAT through a `passt` sidecar (Linux only, M3-03): faster than slirp,
and the guest sees the host's own addresses. Forwards become passt's
`-t`/`-u` options, fixed when the VM starts.

mtu.description: Interface MTU passt advertises; `None` keeps passt's default.

oneOf.description:
Linux: a tap per NIC, attached by the privileged helper to an
existing host bridge the administrator allowlisted (M3-05). Guests
are on the bridge's LAN and reachable directly.

Linux: a tap per NIC on a bridge the helper manages, with no uplink.
The host has an address on it (set in helper.toml); guests reach the
host and each other, not the outside world (M3-05).

Windows: a TAP-Windows adapter, bridged to the LAN (or not) in
Network Connections by an administrator (M3-06).

A private switch inside the daemon (M3-04): VMs on the same isolated
network reach each other and nothing else, with no host or internet
access. Nothing is put on the physical network.

Attached to a network object by id (M3-01). Forwards apply only to
network kinds that take them (NAT).

mac.description: Locally administered MAC; assigned at creation when absent.

queues.description:
Queue pairs (multiqueue). Needs a virtio-net model and a tap-style
backend; absent means one.

virtio.description: virtio-net offload toggles; absent leaves QEMU's defaults.

host_addr.description: Host address to bind; loopback unless deliberately widened.

cpu_max_percent.description: CPU cap in percent of one host core (200 = two full cores).

cpu_weight.description:
Relative CPU share against other VMs, 1–10000 (cgroup `cpu.weight`;
100 is the default share). Linux only.

io.description: Disk IO throttling shared by all of the VM's disks.

memory_max_mib.description:
Hard memory limit for the whole QEMU process in MiB: guest RAM plus
QEMU's own overhead.

ShareSpec.description:
A host folder shared into the guest (M2-13).

Like images, shares never hold host paths: they name a registered
*share root* and a folder relative to it, which the daemon canonicalises
and confines to that root. The guest mounts the share by its tag:
`mount -t 9p -o trans=virtio <tag> /mnt` or `mount -t virtiofs <tag> /mnt`.

path.description: Folder inside the root, `/`-separated; empty for the root itself.

readonly.description: The guest cannot write. Read-only shares always use 9p.

root.description: Name of a registered share root.

tag.description: Mount tag the guest uses (letters, digits, `-`, `_`; up to 31).

TpmSpec.description:
An emulated TPM 2.0 (plan.md §5.1). State lives with the VM; the daemon
runs `swtpm` for it on every start.

UsbPassthrough.description:
A host USB device to pass through, matched the way QEMU's `usb-host`
matches: by vendor and product, optionally narrowed to a bus and port so
two identical devices can be told apart. The guest sees the device
whenever it is plugged in; QEMU waits for it otherwise.

host_bus.description: Linux bus number (`hostbus`); not available on Windows hosts.

host_port.description: Linux port path such as `1.2` (`hostport`); stable per physical port.

label.description: Display name remembered from the host (e.g. "Logitech USB Receiver").

VirtioNetOptions.description: virtio-net feature toggles (M3-07). Each `None` keeps QEMU's default (on).

tso.description:
TCP segmentation offload, IPv4 and IPv6 (`host_tso*`, `guest_tso*`).
Needs checksum offload.

devices.description: Devices added from the palette (M4-05); ids `qui-xdev<N>`.

guest.description: Guest agent channel and cloud-init seed (M7-02/03).

limits.description: CPU, memory and disk IO limits (M6-07).

machine.description: Versioned machine type; aliases are pinned at creation (§5.2).

passthrough.description: Raw argv tokens appended after generated options (§5.3).

shares.description: Host folders shared into the guest (Linux hosts; plan.md §9.6).

tpm.description:
An emulated TPM 2.0 backed by an `swtpm` sidecar (M7-07). Only
available where the probe finds a TPM backend.

usb.description: Host USB devices passed through to the guest (M2-12).

info.description: HTTP API of qemu-uid. Browsers authenticate with a session cookie and send X-CSRF-Token on unsafe methods; other clients send an API token as a Bearer token. WebSocket routes need a single-use ticket from the ticket endpoint.
info.title: qemu-ui API
